result.title: r1 — Adversarial review of the "new structures": operator unification, marked depth, mimicker families, depth/Theorems A–C; chiral-blindness theorem for the ACUE fibre
result.status: complete — review delivered with 9/9 identity checks passing; candidate conjecture refuted as posed and replaced by Theorem E1 (proved) + E2/E3 (computed N=5..8); one open general-N conjecture

claims.statement: Fourier identity sum_d d(N-d) e^{-2pi i k d/N} = -N/(2 sin^2(pi k/N)), L_N e_delta = delta(N-delta) e_delta, L_N = Jacobian of the Coulomb flow at the clock, N^{-1}L_N -> (-Delta)^{1/2}: all STANDARD (finite Fourier transform of a quadratic / Fejer kernel; Hessian of the circular log-gas at the Fekete configuration = phonon spectrum of the trigonometric Calogero-Sutherland lattice (Sutherland 1972, Calogero-Perelomov CMP 1978, recalled); one-magnon sector of Haldane-Shastry (recalled); linearised DBM = fractional heat equation of order 1 (Bourgade-Erdos-Yau-Yin, Landon-Sosoe-Yau, recalled)).
claims.evidence: r1_structure_check.py A-D: deviations 8.5e-12 (sympy exact at N=6,8), 2.0e-12, 2.4e-13, continuum kernel identity to 30 digits.

claims.statement: Exact band-limited identity L_N = N(-Delta)^{1/2} + Delta on trigonometric polynomials of degree <= N/2 sampled on Z_N (symbol N|d| - d^2); the Jacobian identity is a change of variables: d e_j/d theta_m at the clock = i(-1)^{j-1} w^{mj}, so coefficient j is Fourier mode j of the displacement and the diagonal flow rate j(N-j) is the eigenvalue (two-line proof).
claims.evidence: r1_structure_check.py B (6.4e-13) and C (6.8e-10, central differences at N=8); proof written in report §1.2.

claims.statement: The dynamic delta(N-delta) is the SU(N) quadratic Casimir of wedge^delta: C_2(omega_j) = j(N-j)(N+1)/N; hence the finite depth flow P_s = sum a_j e^{s j(N-j)} z^j is the SU(N) heat flow of the class function det(1 - z.) at time t = -sN/(N+1) (backward for s>0). Standard facts, newly connected; identification not known to me in the literature.
claims.evidence: r1_structure_check.py E (1.8e-15, N=3..9); characters are Laplace eigenfunctions (standard, recalled). U(N) Casimir j(N-j+1) shown to add a radial dilation that breaks self-inversiveness, so SU(N) is the right group.

claims.statement: The §2.3 'mechanism' (invisibility degree = relaxation rate, 'impostors hide in the fastest-relaxing modes') is NOT established: the static delta(N-delta) is a lattice aliasing/hop cost for a density mode on configuration space; the dynamic one is a Casimir for a tangent mode at the clock; no intertwining map is given and none was found. Static side itself verified: the sector pairing E_ACUE[z^delta p_lam conj p_nu] first opens at degree exactly delta(N-delta).
claims.evidence: r1_structure_check.py F: (delta, first nonzero degree) = (1,4),(2,6) at N=5; (1,5),(2,8),(3,9) at N=6, with parts<=N and parts<=2N-1. Failed attempt recorded in report §7.1.

claims.statement: Marked-depth rank-two law: the first term is textbook first-order perturbation (Hellmann-Feynman + Cayley chain rule); the second term is the product rule applied to the identity tau = (8 tau/delta^2) delta^2/8, so the reported 11-digit 'parameter-free confirmation' is circular — it holds equally with phi = delta^3 or phi = 1 in place of delta^2/8. Sign convention: d theta/d lambda = +2/(1+lambda^2) (Astra audit correct); the paper's c_j = -2/(1+lambda^2) is compensated by the a/b labelling, formula right iff delta := theta_b - theta_a with b counter-clockwise of a.
claims.evidence: r1_structure_check.py G: Cayley sign 7.3e-12; gap' correct-sign form 1.3e-11; product-rule residual 2.9e-11 / 3.5e-11 / 0 for phi = delta^2/8, delta^3, 1. Legacy scripts reproduced exactly (data/r1_legacy_reproduction.log: corr 1.00000000, residual 5.66e-11, top-2 energy 0.9862, angles 2.26e-6/2.96e-6 deg).

claims.statement: Honest content of the marked-depth law: the constant-kappa local term carries median 91.5% (N=6, 10-90%: 33-100%) and 99.75% (N=8, 97.3-100%) of the response over random configurations and marks; background renormalisation is small and shrinks with N, as Theorem B predicts.
claims.evidence: r1_structure_check.py G, 4 configs x 6 marks per N.

claims.statement: On spectral measures (the only setting of the ACUE programme) the marked depth needs a lift; with the canonical Haar lift and the rotation-covariant marking U -> U e^{i eta uu*}, chi~ = <grad tau, q> with q ~ Dirichlet(1,...,1): first Haar moment = (1/N) sum_j d_j tau = 0 identically (rotation invariance), second = |grad tau|^2/(N(N+1)), higher moments are symmetric polynomials in grad tau. The Cayley marking is not rotation-covariant and its lattice-rotation average also vanishes. The isospectral-pair 'separation' only shows chi(.;u) is not a class function.
claims.evidence: r1_structure_check.py H: chi~ law 3.7e-11 over 300 Haar marks; sum grad 1.5e-11; MC second moment 4.81e-5 vs exact 5.11e-5 (n=300). Proof in report §2.4.

claims.statement: The centre-of-mass family, the det-character/secant family and the parity sectors are ONE family: tilts q = mu G(det U_C) by functions of the determinant (det^2 = e^{2 pi i X/N}, det^N = (-1)^X; every nonnegative g on Z_N is |P_a|^2). Membership in the fibre for mu Re/Im det^{2k} iff k(N-k) > N, i.e. 2 <= k <= N-2. The CUE analogue is trivial (det carries only the global rotation phase, independent of the shape); the lattice quantises the rotation so det^2 becomes a shape invariant. Elementary; new to my knowledge as a family (conservative).
claims.evidence: r1_det_tilt_laws.py: membership matches k(N-k) > N for all k at N=5..8 (residual <= 4e-16 in, >= 1e-2 out); mimicker_fibre.py reproduced (com null dims 2,3,4,5 = cos/sin det^4, cos det^6, ...).

claims.statement: Depth statistic, Coulomb ODE, two-body constant delta^2/8: STANDARD (Polya, de Bruijn, Csordas-Smith-Varga 1994 Lehmer pairs; Rodgers-Tao 2018 §2; Tao blog 'Heat flow and zeroes of polynomials II: zeroes on a circle', 7 June 2018 — existence/title/date verified by one web search, text not fetched). CUE exponent -8/3 is Ben Arous-Bourgade's 4/3 composed with the two-body law (recalled).
claims.evidence: Report §4.1; dihedral invariance of tau checked to 2.8e-16 (r1_structure_check.py I).

claims.statement: Theorem A is correct (circle version of the elementary convexity fact on the line), but its consequence undercuts the paper's tractability claim: under hard-core AH, N^2(-Lambda) >= pi^2/8, so N^2(-Lambda) < pi^2/8 implies delta_min < pi/N — the depth threshold is a strictly stronger hypothesis than the direct gap statement, never easier; the reverse needs the unproved background bound and fails on the lattice (rho_inf >= 1.05). Theorem C(i) is A + pigeonhole; C(ii) remains reduced to Ben Arous-Bourgade plus an open rigidity bound. Strong-LR2019-AH caveat (Astra) applies.
claims.evidence: Report §4.2-4.3; logical consequence of Theorem A as stated in the paper.

claims.statement: 'The depth is smooth in the configuration' (paper §1.5) is false on a positive-mass set: tau is a min over pairs and has kinks where the first collision is tied; kinks found on 3, 4, 6 non-clock orbits at N=5,6,7, all mirror-symmetric configurations.

Theorem E1 (chiral blindness). For N >= 5, 2 <= k <= N-2, |eps| < 1: q_{k,eps} = mu_ACUE (1 + eps Im det(U_C)^{2k}) is a probability measure in the CUE-moment fibre F_N, and every dihedral-invariant statistic (depth, clock atom + law of N^2(-Lambda), |grad tau|^2 and all even Haar moments of any marked depth, pattern counts, |balanced moments| of all degrees) has identical law under q_{k,eps} and mu_ACUE; the same for mu(1 + eps h) for every reflection-odd fibre direction h. The chiral tangent space has dimension 1, 3, 39, 186 at N = 5, 6, 7, 8 (det-type: 1, 1, 2, 2).
claims.evidence: Proof in report §5.1 (R-oddness of mu h and R-invariance of level sets). Numerics r1_fibre_depth_separation.py + r1_det_tilt_laws.py: TV(q,mu) = 0.29/0.30/0.29/0.23-0.27 at eps=0.9 while TV between tau-laws <= 1.3e-15, atom and E[N^2 tau|nc] identical; fibre split 1+1, 7+3, 41+39 (matches handoff's 39/80), 217+186.

claims.statement: On the reflection-symmetric sub-fibre the unmarked depth law (clock atom + law of N^2(-Lambda)) is already a complete invariant at N = 5..8: tau takes distinct values on all 15/49/132/439 reflection classes (min separations 7.6e-5, 2.6e-6, 8.6e-7, 2.0e-7 vs solver 1e-12); law-map rank 1/1, 7/7, 41/41, 217/217. No compression: atom + m power moments see exactly m+1 dimensions (generic), and |grad tau|^2 adds nothing. General-N injectivity (E2') is open.

The reflection-odd third Haar moment of the covariant marked depth, G3 = sum_j (d_j tau)^3, does see one chiral direction (E_q G3 - E_mu G3 = -3.0e-3, +6.7e-3, -6.7e-5 at N = 5, 6, 7 for the explicit chiral impostor while tau-laws coincide to 1e-17), but so does any rotation-invariant reflection-odd statistic outside the degree-<=N span: odd balanced moments of degree N+1 see 1/1, 2/3, 21/39 chiral dims. Nothing is special about the marked depth.

The candidate conjecture of the brief ('the marked-depth rank-two law / polarisation detector separates ACUE from every other fibre element at N = 6, 7') is refuted as posed: (1) ill-posed for spectral measures, (2) blind to the 3- resp. 39-dimensional chiral family including closed-form impostors at TV ~ 0.3, (3) redundant on the symmetric part where the unmarked depth law is already injective. Corrected statement: for N <= 8 the pair (atom, law of N^2(-Lambda)) is a complete invariant of F_N^sym and no dihedral-invariant statistic is an invariant of F_N \ F_N^sym.

The handoff's claim that the functional equation 'kills the chiral half of the fibre at zero cost' requires reversibility of the local limit of the positive-ordinate zero process, which the functional equation does not supply (permutation symmetry of R_n gives R_3(a,b) = R_3(-b,-a), not R_3(a,b) = R_3(-a,-b)); it is an extra hypothesis. Without it the chiral impostors are admissible and the entire depth programme cannot see them.
claims.evidence: Report §5.4 and §8; argument written, no counterexample process constructed.

unresolved: E2': tau injective on reflection classes of lattice orbits for all N (verified N<=8; no non-coincidence argument for first-collision times of non-mirror configurations).
Reversibility of the local limit of the zeta zero process (admissibility of the chiral half of the fibre); not implied by the functional equation.
An intertwiner between density modes z(C)^delta mu on configuration space and tangent modes at the clock that would make the paper's §2.3 mechanism a theorem; none found.
Theorem C(ii): high-probability bound on the background stiffness S for the extremal CUE pair (rigidity estimate), not attempted here.
Whether the SU(N) backward-heat-flow identification of the finite depth flow yields more than a change of language (e.g. a Brownian characterisation of -Lambda).
Literature check of the determinant-tilt family and of the depth/CUE law against arXiv:2308.11685 (surfaced by the single web search, not read); all other citations recalled, not verified.
result.notes: Data and logs: overnight/fable/data/r1_structure_check.log (9 PASS, 0 FAIL), r1_fibre_depth_separation.log, r1_det_tilt_laws.log, r1_legacy_reproduction.log, r1_fibre_N{5,6,7,8}.npz (null spaces, reflection maps, tau, gradients). Legacy scripts (mimicker_fibre.py, marked_depth.py, marked_depth_law.py) reproduce the paper's numbers exactly; the review disputes interpretation, not computation. No pre-existing file was modified; no git commit/push. One web search was made (permitted single attempt) and confirmed only the existence/title/date of Tao's 'Heat flow and zeroes of polynomials II: zeroes on a circle' (7 June 2018); its content was not fetched. Two bugs in my own scripts (delta-q parametrisation of fibre directions; an absolute zero-row filter) were found and fixed before any reported number was recorded (documented in report §7.4). Runtime: ~4 minutes total, single core.
